newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay share index falls 2.75 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Bombay share index falls 2.75 pct at close.

text.p: Bombay blue-chips closed sharply lower on Thursday as profittaking by marketmen erased price gains over the last two sessions, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exhange plunged 91.75 points, or 2.75 percent to a provisional close of 3,250.11. The day's high was 3,344.67.
"The market logic is baffling," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage firm. "Speculators who had built up positions in pivotals are pulling down prices."
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index fell 21.96 points or 2.31 percent to 929.04 provisional.
Traders said hectic selling in frontline stocks dragged the market down as profittakers became active.

"Many stocks which were hit by circuit-breaker limits at close of trade yesterday (Wednesday) bore the brunt of selling pressure on Thursday" said Vijay Pandya, director at Classic Share & Stock Brokers.
Dealers said the fall in share prices was expected after the market had rallied about 6.7 percent in two straight days.
"This seems to be a slight reaction after the profittaking that has set in the market," said Amit Dalal, a BSE broker.
In the list of pivotal stocks, ACC lost 80.70 rupees to 1,565.0, Reliance 5.75 to 209.0, SBI 14.20 to 225.75, TISCO 6.75 to 186.0, TELCO 17.70 to 424.50 and ITC 11.0 to 311.50.
Shares of Boehringer Mannhein fell 7.75 rupees to 78.75 after its unit was closed by authorities on Wednesday, dealers said.
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) shut down the firm's plant near Bombay after tablets manufactured there were found to be contaminated.
